text: {"overall_winner": "A", "qualities": [{"evidence": "Essay A presents a clear thesis with three distinct reasons (danger, blame conflicts, expense) and returns to them in the conclusion", "quality": "Organized argumentative structure", "description": "The essay maintains a clear introduction-body-conclusion structure with a stated position and reasons that are developed and revisited."}, {"evidence": "Essay A develops each point in its own paragraph, such as the extended scenario of a crash between two driverless cars to explore the blame question", "quality": "Elaborated reasoning", "description": "Each claim is unpacked with concrete scenarios and extended explanation rather than being stated briefly."}, {"evidence": "Essay A integrates article details like the 1950s General Motors test track and Berkeley magnets to support the cost argument", "quality": "Integrated textual evidence", "description": "The essay weaves specific details from the source article into its own argument rather than merely referencing the topic."}, {"evidence": "Essay A uses rhetorical questions and hypothetical scenarios (\"Imagine being on the road relaxing...\") to engage the reader", "quality": "Rhetorical engagement", "description": "The essay employs vivid hypotheticals and rhetorical devices to make its argument compelling and concrete."}, {"evidence": "Essay A acknowledges the opposing view (\"driverless cars would be amazing to have\") before rebutting it", "quality": "Counterargument awareness", "description": "The essay concedes the appeal of driverless cars while explaining why the drawbacks outweigh the benefits."}, {"evidence": "Essay B contains frequent spelling and grammar errors such as 'I thnk', 'beacuse', 'indvivle', 'liscene', 'in-danger', 'their safe'", "quality": "Conventional written language", "description": "Essay A demonstrates far stronger control of spelling, grammar, and sentence mechanics than Essay B."}]}
